title: Coherence cascade notes - NVSwitch timeout + ECC residue (evening shift)
content:
Summary:

This is a set of evening-shift notes documenting a recurring, low-signal failure mode we've started calling a 'coherence cascade' — a sequence where a transient NVSwitch/NVLink negotiation delay coincides with small, persistent ECC counter increments on a subset of GPUs, then -- during warm-start of large transformer workloads -- triggers memory corruption that surfaces as soft kernel panics or driver hangs. It's not the classic catastrophic ECC spike; counters are subtle and distributed.

Why this doc: capture observations from two nights of triage (05-11 and 05-13), list commands we ran, lay out hypotheses that differ from prior ECC/eviction failures, and propose a short runbook for oncall to reduce blast radius while we surface reliable telemetry.

Observed symptoms (night shift):
- Multiple requests to the same node stack during model warmup (~first 30s of a long chat session) returned I/O errors or hung; container runtime restarted (runc/cri), leading to pod eviction and resubmit.
- dmesg showed intermittent kernel oops referencing 'nvlink timeout' and later a GPU page-fault traceback in nvidia-driver.
- ECC correctable counters (per-GPU) were elevated relative to baseline but not bursting; each affected GPU had ~10-60 correctable errors over 24h — below historical alert thresholds.
- NVSwitch link retrain events spiked within a 1-2s window for the node; nvlink_peer/query reports showed brief link-down followed by negotiation.
- No immediate PSU or host thermal trip recorded; ambient rack temp +1–2C during incident.

Short timeline (condensed):
- 2026-05-11 21:13 UTC: First user warm-start triggers; 10s later pod shows runtime kill and kernel oops (see logs below).
- 21:14–21:20 UTC: Several automated retries hit same node; SRE route-to-dedicated fallback engaged by hatchery rules.
- 2026-05-13 03:40 UTC: Recurred on a different node in same rack; similar characteristics.

Key log snippets (redacted):
- dmesg: "[  6543.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:5e:00): 31, Graphics Exception on GPU at 0x7f..."
- dmesg: "[  6543.123789] nvidia 0000:5e:00: nvlink: link training timeout, retrying"
- containerd: "failed to start container: exit status 137"

Telemetry/commands we ran:
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,GRAPHICS -i 0,1,2 -> grabbed ECC counters per GPU and historical reset times.
- nvlink --status (internal helper) -> showed transient link-state transitions between fabric ports 0/1 for GPUs 0/1.
- sudo journalctl -k -u kubelet --since "-30m" | grep -E "nvidia|nvlink|NVRM" -> aggregated kernel/driver errors.
- perf and flamegraphs were not useful (OOM/panic before usable profile).

Reproduction attempts and what failed: 
- Stress-testing synthetic kernel using cuBLAS matmul heavy warmup reproduced kernel hang after ~25s in a lab node where we could toggle NVSwitch link delay using driver debug knobs.
- Eviction-replay (simulated eviction/restore) did NOT reliably reproduce unless the node was in the exact thermal/IO window (low ambient change) and multiple warm-start connections were present.

Hypotheses (ordered by current confidence):
1) NVSwitch negotiation latency + slight ECC residue: small correctable ECC accumulation reduces margin for retry; if an NVSwitch link retrain occurs during KV cache warmup (lots of small allocations and DMA), memory metadata gets inconsistent and leads to a GPU-side page fault that the driver can't reconcile -> NVRM Xid 31.
2) Driver-side race introduced after recent 535.x driver backport: a missing fence between nvlink reconfiguration and CUDA context restore that only surfaces under prefetch/warmup patterns.
3) PSU/Vendor firmware oddness causing micro-voltage droop during negotiation -> increases correctable ECC but doesn't trip sensors. Lower confidence because PSU traces didn't show spikes.

Why this differs from previous ECC surges:
- Past events had huge ECC deltas (thousands) and clear thermal/aging signature. This is softer, distributed across more GPUs, paired with NVLink retrain timing, and triggers during workload warmup patterns rather than sustained long-run compute.

Immediate mitigation for oncall (quick, low-risk):
- If you see NVSwitch negotiation timeouts + low-level ECC correctable increases on a node during warm-start failures, temporarily drain the node from the scheduler. Reason: repeated warm-starts will increase exposure and potentially flip correctable->uncorrectable.
- Use the 'host-level fallback' route: re-route latency-sensitive requests away from node to dedicated pool for 5–10m while SRE investigates.
- Increase pod restart backoff to prevent tight retry storms against the same node.

Short-term telemetry & alerting changes (proposed):
- Add a composite SLO alert: NVLink retrain rate > 5/min AND sum(correctable_ecc) over rack > 200 in 1h. Currently we alert only on per-GPU thresholds.
- Add a 'warmstart-failure' log extractor that flags NVRM Xid 31 within 30s of process create for LLM model processes.
- Mark driver version for all nodes in rack and correlate with incidents (we saw two different driver branches with similar symptoms).

Debug notes for next lab repro:
- Reproduce using 2–3 simultaneous warm-starts invoking large KV cache allocation (sequence len 512) to mimic chat model behavior.
- Use driver debug knobs to force nvlink retrain (timing) while simultaneously injecting correctable ECC counts (hardware-in-the-loop or simulated via driver debug).
- Capture full GPU microstate using internal tracing (nvml debug + kernel tracepoints) from 10s before warm-start to 60s after.

Action items (owner, due):
- Omar: build a lightweight extractor that surfaces NVRM Xid 31 + nvlink-retrain within 1m; drop into SRE alerting. Due 2026-05-28.
- Priya: schedule lab window with infra to attempt forced nvlink retrain + warmstart reproduction (need 2 nodes in same switch fabric). Due 2026-05-22.
- Tom: audit driver versions across the fleet and annotate nodes with the recent 535.x backport; escalate to firmware vendor if the lab repro matches. Due 2026-05-24.
- Lila (me): draft a short-runbook for oncall with step-by-step safe-drain and fallback instructions, include sample kubectl commands and how to check nvlink + ECC counters. Due 2026-05-21.

Runbook excerpt (quick ops play):
- Check node health: kubectl describe node <node> -> look for kubelet restarts.
- Check driver/kernel errors: sudo journalctl -k -u kubelet | grep -i nvidia -n 200.
- Pull ECC counters: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC -i <gpu-id>.
- Check nvlink state: /opt/redwood/bin/nvlink-monitor --node <node> (internal tool) or nvlink-cli --status.
- If nvlink retrain + Xid 31 seen: cordon node, drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data, set node to maintenance role in hatchery, notify infra.

Open questions we still have:
- Why do correctable ECC counters remain modest (no burst) but still correlate with the failure window? Are we missing a microsecond-scale transient that correctable counters aggregate and don't expose?
- Is the problem limited to specific NVSwitch firmware versions or a particular board revision?
- Could recent kernel/driver mitigations for power be re-ordering accesses and exposing a new race?

Notes & references:
- Linked incident JIRA-SRE-5781 has raw logs and pod ids.
- PR GH-PR-2347 contains proposed driver fencing patch (not merged).
- Internal lab notes: confluence://sre/gpu-coherence-notes (work-in-progress).

If you're oncall and hit this, ping #sre-gpu with node name + one line: "nvlink-retrain + Xid31 during warmstart, draining now" and follow runbook.

Signed-off: Lila Nguyen (eng-sre).

Appendix: quick commands we used during triage (copy/paste safe):
- sudo journalctl -k | grep -i -E "NVRM|nvlink|Xid" --no-pager -n 200
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERFORMANCE | sed -n '1,200p'
- kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
- kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

(End of notes)
